$comment: Single source of truth for imagery. `npm run manifest` regenerates prompts/image-manifest.md from this file. Drop a real file into public/images/<kind>/<filename> and the placeholder plate is replaced automatically at build time.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A dog asleep in a rectangle of afternoon light in an ordinary room. Quiet, natural, slightly cinematic, a great deal of empty floor.
images.concept: The whole argument of the essay, asleep on a floor.
images.purpose: Hero. Sets the emotional temperature of the book.
images.revision: Negative space is the point — the dog should occupy less of the frame than feels comfortable.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A coffee mug, keys or a pair of glasses sitting exactly where someone put them down. Nothing arranged.
images.concept: The mundane object as evidence that somebody lives here.
images.purpose: Small taped inset. Interrupts the first text spread at a conceptual turn, not for decoration.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A quiet lakeside in flat light. Familiar rather than beautiful — the kind of view someone passes daily.
images.concept: A place you have already stopped seeing.
images.purpose: Pairs with the observational drawing opposite it.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A broad, ordinary view of a path beside water. The photograph anyone would take and nobody would keep.
images.concept: What the place is showing you.
images.purpose: Left half of the pair. Must be genuinely unremarkable.
images.revision: Shoot the detail frame at the same location, same hour, so the pairing is truthful.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A close crop from inside the same view revealing an unexpected pattern: clouds reflected in water, insects on the surface, tree roots, light through leaves.
images.concept: What the place was doing the whole time.
images.purpose: Right half of the pair. The payoff.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: Two people from behind, walking beside water. Unposed, mid-stride, faces not visible.
images.concept: An astonishing biological achievement, being performed absent-mindedly.
images.purpose: Carries the walking passage. Ideal future personal-photo slot.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A shadow falling across pavement — a railing, a branch, a person out of frame.
images.concept: Noticed, not explained.
images.purpose: First of three. Captions record only what was noticed.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A single bird near a shoreline, small in the frame, doing nothing of consequence.
images.concept: Noticed, not explained.
images.purpose: Second of three.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: A dog's nose deep in grass, close and slightly out of focus.
images.concept: Noticed, not explained.
images.purpose: Third of three.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The same tree, or the same stretch of lakeshore, in spring — bare branches breaking. Identical framing, identical position.
images.concept: The route repeats. The world does not.
images.purpose: Frame 1 of four. The frame must not move between visits.
images.revision: Shot from a marked position. If the framing drifts, the spread stops working.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The same tree, or the same stretch of lakeshore, in summer — full canopy, hard light. Identical framing, identical position.
images.concept: The route repeats. The world does not.
images.purpose: Frame 2 of four. The frame must not move between visits.
images.revision: Shot from a marked position. If the framing drifts, the spread stops working.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The same tree, or the same stretch of lakeshore, in autumn — thinning, warm. Identical framing, identical position.
images.concept: The route repeats. The world does not.
images.purpose: Frame 3 of four. The frame must not move between visits.
images.revision: Shot from a marked position. If the framing drifts, the spread stops working.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: The same tree, or the same stretch of lakeshore, in winter — bare, flat light. Identical framing, identical position.
images.concept: The route repeats. The world does not.
images.purpose: Frame 4 of four. The frame must not move between visits.
images.revision: Shot from a marked position. If the framing drifts, the spread stops working.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: Someone standing in kitchen light, seen naturally from behind or partly obscured. Intimate without being staged.
images.concept: The extraordinary person, become the person in the kitchen.
images.purpose: Crossover band. Ideal future personal-photo slot — this one especially.
images.revision: Keep the figure fully on one page. Nothing of interest within 15 mm of the fold.

images.essay: Why Ordinary Days May Be the Point of Life
images.subject: Late-afternoon lake, an empty path, a familiar room, or a dog walking away. Inhabited rather than monumental.
images.concept: The book putting you back down where it found you.
images.purpose: Closing image. Not spectacular — that is the requirement, not a limitation.

images.essay: The Secret Life of Attention
images.subject: A second-floor apartment window at dusk, one of many, the only one lit; the glass carries a faint reflection of the street trees behind the viewer.
images.concept: Two worlds occupying the same surface. You can attend to the room or to the reflection, never both at once.
images.purpose: Sets the essay's premise before a word of it is read.

images.essay: The Secret Life of Attention
images.subject: A field-guide plate of a single room, drawn twice: once complete in fine hairline ink, once as the four or five marks that survived being looked at.
images.concept: The paraphrase. What the editor kept.
images.purpose: Gives the pull quote something to argue with rather than decorate.

images.essay: The Secret Life of Attention
images.subject: An old dog lying at the edge of a rectangle of afternoon light on a wood floor, having moved with it; the previous position still visible as a dent in a rug.
images.concept: Sustained attention without effort. The animal is better at this than you are.
images.purpose: Carries the essay's central practical claim: noticing is a matter of speed, not will.

images.essay: The Secret Life of Attention
images.subject: An enormous flat bank of weather over a grey lake, with one very small figure standing on a breakwater far right of centre.
images.concept: Scale as an attention device. The eye has to travel to find the person.
images.purpose: The book's first long exhale. No text, no folio.
images.revision: Keep the horizon clear of the fold; the figure must sit fully on the recto.

images.subject: Wet sidewalk after rain, a scatter of starlings on a wire above it, arranged by accident into something that reads like handwriting.
images.concept: The world composing itself without intending to.
images.purpose: Opens Part I on an image of a pattern that was always there.

images.essay: The Secret Life of Attention
images.subject: Four strangers at a crosswalk, all looking at four different things, their shadows overlapping into a single shape.
images.concept: Four separate paraphrases of one street corner.
images.purpose: Interrupts the text at the foot of the verso, so the spread has weight where it would otherwise trail off.
